title: Solver Agent: an Agentic AI Framework for Theoretical Physics Computations Applied to F-theory Uplifts of O3-planes and S-folds
abstract: arXiv:2609.35958v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We introduce Solver Agent, an AI framework based on large language models for calculations and proofs in mathematics and theoretical physics. The solution process is tracked through a persistent ledger that records assumptions, derivations, and computations. A central agent delegates tasks to specialized sub-agents, while independent agents verify both intermediate steps and the final result. This setup improves the traceability, reproducibility, and verification of computer-assisted calculations. Applying Solver Agent, we study global F-theory uplifts of Type IIB orientifolds and their S-fold generalizations. We establish sufficient conditions for Weierstrass models over projective threefolds with terminal $\mathbb{Z}_k$ quotient singularities ($k\in\{2,3,4,6\}$) to give $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial projective elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau fourfolds with isolated Gorenstein terminal quotient singularities. These geometries realize O3-plan

translated_title: Solver Agent：一个用于理论物理计算的智能体AI框架及其在O3平面与S-折叠的F理论抬升中的应用
translated_abstract: 我们提出了Solver Agent，一个基于大语言模型的AI框架，用于数学与理论物理中的计算和证明。求解过程通过一个持久化账本进行追踪，该账本记录假设、推导和计算。一个中央智能体将任务分派给专门的子智能体，同时由独立的智能体验证中间步骤与最终结果。这一设置提升了计算机辅助计算的可追溯性、可复现性与可验证性。应用Solver Agent，我们研究了IIB型取向ifold（orientifold）及其S-折叠推广的全局F理论抬升。我们为具有终端 $\mathbb{Z}_k$ 商奇点（$k\in\{2,3,4,6\}$）的射影三维簇上的Weierstrass模型建立了充分条件，使其给出具有孤立Gorenstein终端商奇点的 $\mathbb{Q}$-因子化射影椭圆纤维化Calabi-Yau四维簇。这些几何实现了O3平面…（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出了Solver Agent——一个基于大语言模型、通过中央智能体分派任务、子智能体执行计算、独立智能体验证结果并利用持久化账本记录全过程的多智能体AI框架，显著提升了理论物理计算的可追溯性与可验证性，并将其成功应用于IIB型取向ifold及S-折叠的全局F理论抬升，建立了带终端商奇点的Weierstrass模型给出Q-因子化椭圆纤维化Calabi-Yau四维簇的充分条件。
en_tdlr: We introduce Solver Agent, an agentic AI framework based on LLMs that uses a central agent, specialized sub-agents, independent verification agents, and a persistent ledger to improve traceability and verifiability of theoretical physics computations, and apply it to establish sufficient conditions for global F-theory uplifts of Type IIB orientifolds and S-folds with terminal quotient singularities.
